PSG: Passing. Used in NOTAM text to indicate that a condition or event is passing or has passed a specified location.
PSN: Position. Used in aviation communications and NOTAM text to refer to a geographical location or coordinate.
PSP: Paved stopway. A rectangular paved surface at the end of a runway designated for aircraft to stop during an aborted take-off, providing additional safety beyond the runway end.
PSR: Primary surveillance radar. A ground-based radar system that detects aircraft by measuring the bearing and range of reflected radio signals from the aircraft's skin, without requiring any onboard transponder equipment.
PTN: Procedure turn. A maneuver prescribed in instrument approach procedures to reverse the aircraft's direction, typically used when intercepting the final approach course from an initial approach fix.
PTS: Prior to service. Used in NOTAM and maintenance communications to indicate that a status applies before a particular service or action is carried out.
PWR: Power. Refers to electrical power supply or engine power settings in aviation operations and NOTAM text.
QDM: Magnetic heading to a station. A Q-code used in aviation radio communications to request or report the magnetic heading required to fly directly to a radio navigation aid (e.g., NDB or VOR station), assuming zero wind.
QDR: Magnetic bearing from a station. A Q-code used in aviation radio communications to request or report the magnetic bearing of an aircraft from a radio navigation aid, measured from the station outward.
QFE: Atmospheric pressure at aerodrome elevation. A Q-code used in aviation radio communications for the barometric pressure setting that, when set on the altimeter sub-scale, causes the altimeter to read zero (or aerodrome elevation) when the aircraft is on the runway.
QFU: Magnetic orientation of runway. A Q-code used in aviation radio communications to request or report the magnetic direction of a runway in use, expressed in degrees magnetic.
QNH: Altimeter sub-scale setting to obtain elevation. A Q-code used in aviation radio communications for the barometric pressure setting that, when set on the altimeter sub-scale, causes the altimeter to display the aerodrome elevation when the aircraft is on the ground at that aerodrome.
R: Red. A color used in aviation lighting systems, including runway edge lights, obstruction lights, and visual approach slope indicators (PAPI/VASI). Also used as a prefix for Restricted Areas in airspace classification.
RA: Radio altimeter. An aircraft instrument that uses radio waves to measure the actual height above the terrain directly below the aircraft, essential for low-visibility approaches, auto-land systems, and Ground Proximity Warning Systems (GPWS).
RAB: Repair and base (status). Used in NOTAM and maintenance reports to indicate that an item or facility is under repair and is in a base/out-of-service status.
RAC: Rules of the air and air traffic control. The set of international regulations governing the conduct of flight operations, air traffic control procedures, and aircraft separation standards, as defined by ICAO Annex 2.
RACH: Radiocommunication failure. A NOTAM code indicating a loss or degradation of radio communication capability between an aircraft and ground stations or between ground facilities.
RAD: Radiological. Pertaining to radioactive materials or radiation hazards, used in NOTAM text to indicate the presence of radiological conditions or cargo.
RAG: Runway arresting gear. A mechanical system installed at the end of some runways designed to decelerate and stop an aircraft by engaging its tailhook or other capture device during an emergency overrun or aborted take-off.
RALL: Runway alignment indicator lights. A lighting system that provides visual alignment guidance to pilots during the approach, typically consisting of sequenced flashing lights leading to the runway threshold.
RAP: Radar arrival procedure. A standard instrument arrival procedure in which aircraft are vectored by radar to the final approach course, providing efficient traffic sequencing and separation during arrival operations.
RASH: Rash. Used in NOTAM text to describe the rapid onset or spread of a condition or phenomenon, often relating to weather or operational status.
RASN: Rain and snow. An ICAO weather code indicating mixed precipitation of rain and snow falling simultaneously, which can affect visibility and runway conditions.
RAT: Rocket-assisted take-off. A take-off method using auxiliary rocket motors (JATO bottles) strapped to the aircraft to provide additional thrust for short-field or high-altitude take-offs, commonly used by military transport aircraft.
RAZB: Runway azimuth. The magnetic or true bearing of a runway centerline, used in navigation and approach procedure design.
RB: Replaced by. Used in NOTAM text and aviation documentation to indicate that one item, facility, or procedure has been superseded or substituted by another.
RBLS: Retro-reflective (lighting). A type of lighting or marking material that reflects light back toward its source, used on runway and taxiway markers to enhance visibility for pilots during low-light conditions.
RC: Report of correction. A NOTAM or aviation message code indicating that a previously issued report or notice has been corrected.
RCC: Rescue coordination centre. A facility responsible for organizing and coordinating search and rescue (SAR) operations within a specific region, managing resources and communications during aviation emergency situations.
RCF: Radiocommunication failure. A NOTAM code indicating a failure or outage of radio communication equipment or services affecting air-ground or ground-ground communications.
RCH: Reachable. Used in NOTAM and flight planning to indicate that a point, facility, or altitude can be attained within the aircraft's capabilities or fuel range.
RCL: Runway centre line. The physical or painted centerline marking on a runway surface, used to guide aircraft during take-off, landing, and taxiing operations.
RCLL: Runway centre line lights. A series of lights embedded along the runway centerline to provide visual guidance to pilots during take-off and landing, particularly in low-visibility conditions (LVP).
RDN: Radiation. Used in NOTAM text to indicate the presence or risk of radiation hazards, including from cargo, equipment, or environmental sources.
RE: The latest. Used in NOTAM and aviation text to indicate the most recent time, occurrence, or version (e.g., RE = the latest information available). Distinguished from 'RE' meaning 'regarding' by context.
REC: Receive or receiver. Used in aviation communications and NOTAM text to refer to radio reception capability or the receiver component of a communication or navigation system.
REDL: Runway edge lights. A series of lights placed along both edges of a runway to define its lateral boundaries during low-visibility operations, typically white for the main runway and amber for the last 2,000 feet (caution zone).
REF: Reference to or refer to. Used in NOTAM text and aviation documentation to direct the reader to another document, message, or source of information.
REG: Registration. The alphanumeric identifier assigned to an aircraft by its country of registry, used for identification in all aviation communications and documentation.
REIL: Runway end identification lights. A pair of synchronized flashing lights located at the runway threshold, providing rapid and positive identification of the runway end during approach, particularly in low-visibility or cluttered environments.
REP: Report or reporting. Used in aviation communications and NOTAM text to indicate the action of providing information, position reports, or status updates to ATC or other facilities.
RERR: Reroute or rerouted. Used in NOTAM and flight plan management to indicate that an aircraft has been assigned a different route from the originally planned or cleared routing.
RESA: Runway end safety area. A cleared, graded, and obstacle-free area beyond the runway end, designed to reduce the risk of damage to aircraft that undershoot, overrun, or veer off the runway surface.
REST: Restricted or restriction. Used in NOTAM text to indicate limitations or constraints on the use of airspace, facilities, procedures, or equipment.
RF: Radio facility. A general term for any ground-based or airborne radio communication or navigation facility, including VOR, NDB, ILS, and communication transceivers.
RFS: Ready for start-up. A phrase used in ATC communications to indicate that an aircraft is prepared to begin engine start procedures, typically in response to a push-back or start-up clearance request.
RGL: Regulating. Used in NOTAM text to describe the act of controlling or adjusting a system, service, or flow (e.g., regulating traffic flow or regulating facility output).
RLLBL: Releasable. Used in NOTAM and maintenance communications to indicate that an item, system, or component is available for release back to service after maintenance or inspection.
RNP: Required navigation performance. A performance-based navigation specification that defines the accuracy, integrity, continuity, and functionality required for aircraft navigation within a specific airspace, enabling more efficient routing and reduced separation minima.
RO: Routine. Used in NOTAM text to classify a notice as routine (non-urgent) in nature, as opposed to urgent or immediate-action NOTAMs.
